what_happened: An operator changed the config by hand. They set [parallel] max_concurrency to 2, so the queue drain runs plan groups two at a time. The feature (parallel jobs, #120) shipped with the value at 1. Plan groups have existed since #121. The operator chose 2 because that fits the disk until a later change (4e4r) releases build output. No job failed and nothing was rejected. This was a deliberate tuning step.
cause: Athena ships parallelism with a fixed conservative default and has no model of how much disk each running job uses. The safe concurrency level therefore depends on an operator's judgment about free space, and the setting is not tied to what the build output actually takes. Build output is not released after a job, so each extra concurrent job costs disk, and the limit stays a guess. If the guess is wrong, disk fills and the verifier cannot run (see the verifier-environment class).
prevention: Before starting each plan group, the drain should check free disk against a configured per-job reserve. It should lower or defer concurrency below max_concurrency when the space is short, and log that it did so. Releasing build output after each job (4e4r) would also reduce the per-job cost. With both in place, max_concurrency becomes a ceiling and the operator no longer has to size it against the disk by hand.
proposed_request: Make the queue drain protect itself against running out of disk when it runs jobs in parallel. Before it starts each plan group, it should check free disk space against a configurable per-job reserve in athena.toml (for example [parallel] min_free_disk_per_job). If space is short, it should run fewer jobs at once, down to one, rather than the full max_concurrency. It should record in the drain log why it ran fewer. Keep max_concurrency as the upper limit. Add tests showing the drain reduces concurrency when free space is low and uses the full max_concurrency when space is plentiful. Update the docs for the new setting.
